uncertain_sources: The lecture uses Gaussian normal coordinates for point-centered normal coordinates; the chapter preserves the lecture term while stating the pointwise theorem accurately.
The four-dimensional coefficient count is presented as a structural check, while local existence is assigned to the normal-coordinate theorem.
Vanishing Riemann curvature is stated as a local flatness condition so global topology is not inadvertently excluded.
The board's curvature sign and index order are preserved by pairing the commutator definition with the explicit Riemann formula.
A spoken derivative-order slip is normalized: the Riemann tensor contains first derivatives of the connection and therefore second derivatives of the metric.
The uniform gravitational field is treated as an ideal local approximation; realistic isolated-source fields vary and produce tides.
